pages.text: Addendum for $(l:blocks/cinderglee)$(c)$(o)Cinderglee$().$(br)$(br)It is sometimes called the 'Paradox Flame'. Fairly so, after all, it is a fire that seemingly doesn't consume fuel to burn. Of course, in reality, it does burn 'existence'. At least, that's the term I decided to use, but I am still not sure if it's necessarily correct. Hearing that something burns 'existence' is quite confusing, as even understanding what

'that' could be is complicated. Yet, I cannot come up with a better way to describe it. If the Cinderglee touches a living being, it slowly drives it closer and closer to death. It's not like normal fire, in the sense of it burning their body away. It's also not purely decay, as there is no deconstruction involved. Somehow, it burns the living being's very concept, their right to exist in this world. Not the body's right to exist, as that still remains after death, but the actual being's

life. Normally, living should be connected to the functioning of the body or in special cases - such as the undead - the presence of an alternate force. Despite that, Cinderglee ignores that correlation and affects the existence of said being's life or undeath directly. At the same time, this disastrous force is completely inert when faced with anything not alive in some form. The only exception being the plague's Remains or Organic Matter. Those burn with the visible 'smoke' that's given off

when a living being's existence is burning too. I still lack a concrete answer on why that may be, but my best guess so far is that it might be some sort of purification. That is one of the uses fire has as a tool, and with how Cinderglee works specifically, it would make sense for it to be a 'life purifier'. Although how exactly that benefits the plague is still a question for me... Either way, I have to be careful. A fire that doesn't burn hot or cold is dangerously difficult to avoid;
and I have already consumed more Organic Matter than I should have...
